ICP's founder calling out NEAR for "fake decentralization" is funny, because ICP itself is a perfect example of the common "DeCenTraLiZeD!" delusion, which is way too commonplace in the cryptocurrency space: from centralized Ethereum competitors, to centralized universal L2s on Ethereum, and even "decentralized social" projects like Farcaster, which were always centralized.

This is an attack on real decentralization.

Look at ICP. ICP says you own your data. Running a node takes a dual-EPYC server with 512GB RAM and 32TB of NVMe in a data center, plus a DAO vote with proof of identity. I'd laugh but it's just sad at this point. That same DAO can vote to remove content.

The L2s aren't much better. Most still run a single sequencer that can refuse your transaction, and L2beat says some of their "escape hatches" can't actually force anything in. Farcaster just swapped out its only two outside validators.

The point is, THE TEST IS SIMPLE: can a normal person run a node on their laptop, and can anyone vote your posts away? If the answers are no and yes, it's not decentralized. Bitcoin and Ethereum pass, because their chains are small enough for most people to run.

Onchain social has the same problem: if normal people can't run a node, a few approved operators own the network. The problem is all content gets stored in a blockchain, which is frankly absurd. It can't scale: every node has to store every post, so the more people use it, the bigger the node gets, and the fewer people can run one. That's why Bitsocial is pure P2P: a node runs on a Raspberry Pi and only stores the communities it follows.

The elephant in the room is: why are projects like ICP and Farcaster allowed to market themselves as "decentralized" or even "sufficiently decentralized" in the first place, when they really are not? It's VERY misleading. There are billions of dollars of people's life savings in it.

This is one of the major reasons why crypto sucks.

Make crypto cypherpunk again.

item.title: Economic bubbles have been boons to human progress. — 10 replies — 39.2/hr
item.content:encoded:
Economic bubbles have been boons to human progress.

Open thread • Replies: 10 • Updated: 2026-10-25 21:48 UTC

OP

Economic bubbles have been boons to human progress. The canal building bubble, which you could argue is the first truly modern bubble boomed, then bust. And the infrastructure that was built is still paying dividends centuries later. Even though all the companies that built them went bankrupt.
The rail bubble happened in the 1800s, and the companies involved in it that built the rail infrastructure went bankrupt, but their infrastructure is still paying dividends almost two centuries later.
The great depression, which during it, there was a speculative boom in electrification, automotive, radio, built the infrastructure that was the foundation of the modern world.
The dotcom bubble built the infrastructure that enabled the modern internet. The fibre optic infrastructure that was laid during it was extremely capital and labour intensive because everywhere it was laid, the ground had to be dug up. It's still paying dividends three decades later and the internet depends on this infrastructure. Those cables are going to be good for a very long time, and modernising it, they just replace equipment on the ends of the cables.
the real estate bubble during the GFC, if it hadn't happened the housing shortage right now would be a 20 million home shortage instead of 3 million.

These bubbles, they involved pain in the short term, but in the long term they really paid off even if the companies that built these things weren't around anymore to reap the benefits.

If there wasn't an overbuild, and a bust, much of this infrastructure would have been too expensive to scale its uses. But because the companies that owned the infrastructure went bankrupt, the assets were sold for pennies on the dollar, and dirt cheap infrastructure enables innovation that wasn't even imaginable at the time it was built.

We got fucked over by there not being an atomic energy bubble. Try to imagine what essentially free electricity would enable. We should have already been living in that world.
